title: Analysis: Elon Musk's Terafab chases 10 chip iterations a year — can it rival TSMC?
key_facts: At a Tesla X Takeover event in Austin on 11 Oct 2026 Elon Musk said "I don't know how to make chips" and "We'll figure it out".
Terafab aims for 10 chip design iterations a year against about one generation every two years in the industry.

Terafab was announced in March 2026 with an initial investment over US$15 billion; first phase US$16.8 billion in Grimes County, Texas, with construction starting around 1 Dec 2026 and first phase done by end of 2028.
Intel joined in April 2026 as manufacturing partner but financial terms and continued participation remain subject to later agreements.
A 3nm photomask set can cost US$5 million to US$20 million.
Musk gave no specific timeline, saying it could take several years.
quote_evidence: Speaking to more than 2,000 Tesla owners and investors at the X Takeover event held at Tesla's Gigafactory in Austin, Texas, on October 11, Elon Musk made a candid admission: "To be clear, I don't know how to make chips."
The companies have so far agreed only to a general framework, and financial terms, intellectual property rights, and the continued participation of Intel and Tesla remain subject to later agreements.
why_it_matters_hint: Faster test cycles would only help if mask and tape-out costs can be controlled.
notes: Analysis of an 11 Oct event; framed as aspiration.
